However, I can't work out how to transform the R-N value (number of individuals per site) into an occupancy value. I also would like to test the goodness of fit of the R-N models, but can't find an equivalent of the mb.gof.test. Any help or guidance would be much appreciated.

parts:
Dear Tom,

no, unmarked won't give you SEs and CIs for psi as a derived quantity in an RN occupancy model. You have to get those yourself. At least three solutions:
(1) use the delta rule: have to look up/derive/ask somebody what the delta rule approximation for this function of lambda is
(2) use a sort of pseudobootstrap: draw 10000 or so samples from the normal distribution given by the MLE and the SE of lambda (have to backtransform, too, in case you're modeling on log scale) and then apply the transformation to each of them. Take sample mean, SD and 2.5/97.5 percentile as point estimate of psi and its SE and CI. This assumes normality of the estimator, which MLEs have in "large" samples and should work pretty well in most cases
(3) repeat the analysis in JAGS and there, with MCMC samples, it's all very trivial

Best regards  ---- Marc

On Thursday, September 13, 2018 at 2:29:21 PM UTC+8, Kery Marc wrote:
Dear Tom,

no, unmarked won't give you SEs and CIs for psi as a derived quantity in an RN occupancy model. You have to get those yourself. At least three solutions:
(1) use the delta rule: have to look up/derive/ask somebody what the delta rule approximation for this function of lambda is
(2) use a sort of pseudobootstrap: draw 10000 or so samples from the normal distribution given by the MLE and the SE of lambda (have to backtransform, too, in case you're modeling on log scale) and then apply the transformation to each of them. Take sample mean, SD and 2.5/97.5 percentile as point estimate of psi and its SE and CI. This assumes normality of the estimator, which MLEs have in "large" samples and should work pretty well in most cases
(3) repeat the analysis in JAGS and there, with MCMC samples, it's all very trivial

Best regards  ---- Marc
